(B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
3-501.19: Facility has a time as control policy for their food items along the prep line. This time as control is monitored by time records on a magnetic strip. Upon start of inspection, these times had not been updated. When this was brought up to the manager, they immediately corrected the violation. Ensure that time as control records are up to date when the product is placed on the prep line. 
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 Upon arrival the person in charge (PIC) was unable to produce information pertaining to employee health policy. When advised signed reporting agreements were available per the previous inspector's notes in the last inspection report dated 6/19/19 the PIC wasn't sure to which form the inspector was referring. A binder is present in the office that has employee health documentation along with food manager certifications and allergen awareness certifications. Inspector found the necessary paperwork, and PIC was educated as to the significance of documentation. Store manager arrived during and is knowledgeable on all requirements. Store manager was advised to ensure proper education of all management.
Proper handwashing technique was observed to be an issue at the time of inspection today (see #8 for details). All staff, including the PIC upon arrival of inspector, were advised as to proper technique and later observed washing hands properly. Store manager was advised to reiterate proper handwashing with all staff and ensure proper handwashing between tasks. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employees were observed washing hands without proper technique. One employee was observed shutting off the manual faucet without a barrier prior to drying hands. Another employee started to dry his hands, shut off the manual faucet, and then continued to dry his hands with the same paper towels. Also, the shift manager was observed turning off the faucet with a paper towel but did not dry his hands. Hand antiseptic was applied to wet hands prior to drying with paper towels. All three employees were advised as to proper handwashing upon observation of the abovementioned practices. Proper handwasing was later observed. Store manager was advised to re-educate all staff on proper technique. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Hands should be thoroughly dried prior to using the paper towels to shut off the faucet. If additional drying of hands is needed, then retrieve a new paper towel to finish drying hands instead of continuing to use the paper towels just used to shut off the faucet.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: The person in charge at the time of the inspection does not have proof of successful completion of a certified food protection manager course. There is another employee at the time of the inspection who does have this certification, but under the FDA Food Code guidelines, the person in charge is required to have this certificate. Tanner reports he completed the course in July but does not have his certificate on site at the time of the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed a small portion cup being used as a scoop and stored in the cinnamon sugar container next to the fryer. In use utensils stored in the food must have a handle with the handle stored extended up and out of the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 ?F. Reference 3-304.12.
